stories.headline: Pujari blames BJD’s ‘failure’ for flood
stories.title: Pujari blames BJD’s ‘failure’ for flood
stories.summary: Odisha Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari dismisses BJD chief Naveen Patnaik’s "man-made flood" claims, attributing recent disaster impacts to long-standing governance failures and unprecedented rainfall during Cyclone Arnab.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Odisha Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari dismisses BJD chief Naveen Patnaik’s "man-made flood" claims, attributing recent disaster impacts to long-standing governance failures and unprecedented rainfall during Cyclone Arnab.

Bhubaneswar: Joining the ongoing debate over Biju Janata Dal president Naveen Patnaik’s description of the recent flood as man-made, Odisha minister Suresh Pujari on Thursday blamed the previous BJD government’s “failure” to implement mitigation measures during its 24-year rule for the disaster.
Pujari, the Revenue and Disaster Management Minister, also claimed that no loss of life was reported in three cyclones after the BJP came to power in the State two years ago.

However, according to officials, of the 11 deaths and six people reported missing following Cyclone Arnab, 10 people died in landslides in Ganjam and Kandhamala districts, while one man was swept away in floodwaters in Gajapati district.
Pujari said, “I have high regard for Naveen Babu, who was the chief minister for 24 years.

But do you have any answer on the loss of human lives in calamities during the BJD tenure?” The flood management by the Mohan Charan Majhi government is certainly the best in the recent past, as no human casualties were reported in Cyclone Arnab and the floods, except in landslides, he told reporters.
“As many as 9,866 people died in the 1999 Super Cyclone during the Congress period.
Seventy-two people lost their lives in Cyclone Titli, 45 in Cyclone Phailin, and 65 in Fani under the BJD tenure,” Pujari said.
He said the Majhi government has faced three cyclones—Dana, Mantha and Arnab—during its 28 months in office.
Pujari said there is no such scientific forecast or prediction of landslides in India.
“However, we are undertaking studies on such incidents to avoid human casualties in future,” he said.

Rejecting the Opposition’s allegations of a “man-made flood” in Ganjam, Pujari said the State government was prepared for a detailed debate on the matter in the Assembly, which commences on November 18.

stories.headline: Search operations launched across south Kashmir
stories.title: Search operations launched across south Kashmir
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 12: Security forces on Thursday launched and intensified search operations across south Kashmir in the wake of the terror attack on a CRPF checkpoint near Mir Bazar in Kulgam district, even as the joint cordon-and-search operation at the main site entered its second day with an expanded area under cordon. The primary operation, which was suspended overnight due to darkness, resumed at first light in the Nowpora Akhran area. Additional forces have been deployed, barricades strengthened and vehicle checks intensified along the Srinagar-Jammu National Highway and approach roads to seal escape routes. Armoured vehicles and Quick Reaction Teams remain in position as teams comb the forested and rural belts. GOC 15 Corps, Lieutenant General Balbir Singh, visited the spot to review the operations and take stock of the ground situation. Senior officers of the Army, CRPF, and J&K Police are supervising the search, which is being guided by human and technical intelligence inputs. Parallel search and area-domination efforts have been activated at multiple locations across south Kashmir as part of a coordinated response. The attack occurred around 2:15 pm on Wednesday when two heavily armed assailants emerged from a dense cluster of trees and opened fire on a CRPF naka of the 46th Battalion, deployed as a bridge guard roughly 1 to 2 km off the Srinagar-Jammu National Highway near Mir Bazar. Security personnel returned fire, but the attackers fled into the adjoining forested area. The injured personnel have been identified as Head Constable Somveer Singh (Madhya Pradesh), Constable RakeshDass (Assam) and Constable Santosh Chandru (West Bengal). Somveer Singh sustained a bullet injury to his arm and RakeshDass to his leg; both were reported stable. Chandru suffered gunshot wounds to the abdomen and spine and was initially critical. Two of the injured personnel have since been discharged from hospital after treatment. The critically injured jawan was airlifted to the 92 Base Hospital in Srinagar for advanced care. Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha visited the hospital to enquire about his condition and interacted with the treating doctors. Deputy Commissioner Anantnag Bilal Mohiuddin had earlier visited the injured at GMC Anantnag. This is the third terror-related incident reported in south Kashmir in recent months. Forces have maintained a tight vigil across the region while the expanded searches continue.

stories.headline: Permanent peace requires dialogue with strong security response: Arjun Singh Raju
stories.title: Permanent peace requires dialogue with strong security response: Arjun Singh Raju
stories.summary: Ramban, Nov 12: Ramban MLA Arjun Singh Raju has strongly condemned the attack on CRPF personnel in Kashmir, expressing concern over the continued cycle of violence in Jammu and Kashmir and calling for a comprehensive approach to restore lasting peace in the region. Expressing solidarity with the injured personnel, Raju prayed for their speedy recovery and described the attack as a cowardly act aimed at disturbing peace and stability in the Valley. Three CRPF personnel were injured in the incident and are undergoing treatment. He alleged that Pakistan-sponsored terrorists and their over-ground workers continued to remain active in Kashmir and were attempting to disrupt the peaceful atmosphere in the region. He called for a strong response against those involved in terrorist activities. At the same time, Raju emphasised that the recurring incidents of violence and bloodshed must come to an end, observing that merely condemning such attacks through statements would not resolve the situation. "The bloodshed has to stop somewhere. For the last 25 to 30 years, people have been witnessing the killing of security personnel and civilians. We cannot allow this cycle of violence to continue indefinitely," he said. The MLA urged the central government to conduct regular and comprehensive security reviews and strengthen coordination between security agencies and the elected government in Jammu and Kashmir. He observed that managing the security situation entirely from Delhi was difficult and stressed that the involvement of the elected government and local representatives was essential for effective coordination and a better understanding of ground realities. Advocating dialogue alongside a firm security response, Raju said that lasting peace could not be achieved through military action alone and that diplomatic efforts were equally necessary to address long-standing issues between India and Pakistan. Referring to the 1971 war, the Shimla Agreement, the Kargil conflict and the subsequent Agra Summit, he said that dialogue had remained an important means of resolving disputes even after military confrontations. "Bullets may be necessary to deal with terrorism, but permanent peace requires dialogue. If we want lasting peace, we have to sit at the negotiating table and initiate a meaningful dialogue process," he said. Referring to the Pahalgam terror attack and the subsequent military response, Raju questioned whether military action alone could bring a permanent end to terrorism and recurring violence. He maintained that the issue should not be viewed through a political perspective, stressing that protecting innocent lives and ensuring lasting peace in Jammu and Kashmir should remain the priority. Calling for a two-pronged strategy, Raju urged the Centre to take firm action against terrorism while simultaneously exploring diplomatic avenues to address contentious issues with Pakistan. "We do not want innocent people to continue losing their lives on our soil. There must be a decisive effort to stop this bloodshed. A strong security response and meaningful dialogue must go hand in hand if we want permanent peace," he said.

stories.headline: 'Criminal Law Moves Fast Against Poor, But Not Influential': Madras High Court As Centre Sanctions Prosecution Of 2 IAS Officers
stories.title: 'Criminal Law Moves Fast Against Poor, But Not Influential': Madras High Court As Centre Sanctions Prosecution Of 2 IAS Officers
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Secretary to Government, Department of Personnel and Training, has informed the Madras High Court that the Central Government has accorded sanction to prosecute two IAS officers in connection with the tender irregularities scam.
When the matter came up for hearing, Justice Anand Venkatesh was informed that the Centre had accorded sanction to prosecute the two officers – KS Kandasamy and K Vijaya Karthikeyan.
The court was also informed that the investigating agency would be acting upon the sanction and take steps to conduct an investigation against the officers and file a final report.

Taking note of the sanction, the judge orally remarked that the present case was a classic example of how the criminal law worked in the country where the law moved fast against the poor but needed a push when the case related to influential people.
“Classic case of how criminal law works in this country.
See how much effort has been put in by so many people.
Things move fast for poor people.
But for influential people, we have to push and push, and ultimately we are here,” the court orally remarked.
The court was hearing a contempt petition filed by NGO Arappor Ayakkam against the delay in proceedings against former Minister SP Velumani and three IAS officers in a tender irregularities case.
SP Velumani is accused of abusing his official position while he was serving as the Minister for Municipal Administration.
It is alleged that he had extended large-scale favouritism while awarding tenders for road works in Chennai Corporation and Coimbatore Municipal Corporation to his relatives and his close associates.
Arappor Iyakkam, an NGO, made a complaint with the DVAC.

stories.headline: India's Journey of Discovery and Innovation in Space
stories.title: India's Journey of Discovery and Innovation in Space
stories.summary: BEYOND THE SKY Space has always inspired human curiosity. From observing the stars to developing spacecraft, generations have sought to understand the universe and humanity's place within it. Today, advances in scientific research and technology are making it possible to explore space in ways once considered beyond reach. India is now an active part of this wider journey of discovery, with its space programme entering an important new phase. India's early space research began with modest facilities and ambitious scientific goals. On 21 November 1963, a research rocket carrying instruments to study the upper atmosphere was launched from Thumba in Kerala. India's first indigenous sounding rocket followed in 1967. Such rockets carry scientific instruments into the atmosphere to collect information. These early initiatives helped develop the knowledge and experience needed for a long-term space programme. Vikram Sarabhai, recognised as the father of India's space programme, believed that space technology could help address practical needs on Earth. His vision placed importance on communication, education, weather forecasting and the responsible use of scientific knowledge. That approach continues to influence the development of space technology. The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) has developed rockets and satellites that support communication, navigation, weather forecasting and early warnings of natural disasters. Its scientific missions have also contributed to the understanding of the Moon, Mars and the Sun. Chandrayaan-3 reached the Moon's southern high-latitude region on 23 August 2023, and its Pragyan rover conducted scientific studies on the lunar surface. Mangalyaan entered Mars orbit in September 2014, while Aditya-L1 reached its observing position in January 2024 to study the Sun. The space sector is also seeing growing participation from private Indian companies, which are contributing to the development of launch vehicles, satellites, engines and space-based services. This wider participation is creating opportunities for engineers, scientists, researchers and young entrepreneurs. Among the companies working in this field is Skyroot Aerospace, founded in Hyderabad in 2018. In November 2022, its Vikram-S rocket completed a suborbital test flight, demonstrating its rocket technology without placing a satellite into orbit. On 18 July 2026, the company's Vikram-1 made its maiden orbital launch, placing two satellites, Skyroot's SCOPE and Grahaa Space's SOLARAS S3, into low Earth orbit. An orbital launch, on the other hand, gives a satellite the speed and direction needed to continue travelling around Earth. These missions marked important stages in the development of Skyroot's launch vehicles. Agnikul Cosmos, based in Chennai, is developing small rockets designed to carry satellites. In May 2024, it tested Agnibaan SOrTeD using a single-piece engine made through 3D printing, a process in which an object is built layer by layer from a digital design. The flight was a suborbital technology test. Such experiments demonstrate how research, engineering and careful testing help turn ideas into practical systems. The wider space industry also includes companies working beyond rockets. Pixxel has launched six Firefly satellites that capture detailed images of Earth using hyperspectral imaging, a technology that collects information across many different wavelengths of light. Dhruva Space is developing satellite platforms and related systems. Bellatrix Aerospace is working on propulsion technologies that help spacecraft move in orbit. Digantara's SCOT satellite began operations in March 2025 to track objects orbiting Earth. GalaxEye launched its Drishti satellite on 3 May 2026, combining optical imaging with synthetic aperture radar (SAR) technology. Behind every satellite is a network of people, equipment and knowledge. Cameras, computers, electrical systems, communication links, ground stations and software all contribute to a successful mission. This creates work in electronics, manufacturing, design, testing, programming and data analysis. The space sector is therefore not limited to astronauts and rocket scientists. It also depends on people with many different skills. Space technology has practical uses in everyday life. Satellite images can help farmers understand crop conditions and researchers monitor forests, rivers and glaciers. Weather information supports preparations for storms and floods. The NASA–ISRO NISAR mission, launched in July 2025, uses radar to observe changes on Earth and support research into ecosystems, ice and natural hazards. These applications show how studying space can also help people understand and care for their home planet. Public institutions and private companies have complementary responsibilities in this developing field. ISRO contributes scientific experience, research and launch infrastructure. The Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre, known as IN-SPACe, supports and authorises private-sector space activities. Private firms contribute new designs, investment and business ideas. Cooperation between research institutions, universities and industry can help make scientific knowledge useful in practical ways. Universities and research centres will remain important to this progress. Institutions such as the Indian Institutes of Technology and the Indian Institute of Science train students and support research in engineering and science. Young people can participate in this field in many ways. They may design a sensor, develop software, build a component or study satellite images. A classroom science project or a first look through a telescope can become the beginning of a lifelong interest in science. India is also preparing for human spaceflight through the Gaganyaan programme. It is developing systems intended to carry astronauts safely into space and bring them back. Its first uncrewed experimental mission will carry the half-humanoid robot Vyommitra. Indian astronaut Shubhanshu Shukla has also visited the International Space Station, where he completed seven microgravity experiments, adding valuable experience to the country's human-spaceflight programme. In the years ahead, further developments may emerge in reusable rockets, groups of small satellites working together and robotic missions to explore the Moon and other celestial bodies. These are areas of continuing research and development. Their progress will depend on careful planning, scientific understanding, repeated testing and the responsible use of technology. Space exploration is a journey of continuous learning and progress. Every mission requires investment, specialised skills and careful preparation. Each test adds to scientific understanding, with every outcome providing valuable lessons that help engineers develop better technologies. As more objects enter orbit, advances in space monitoring and responsible practices can help make the space environment safer and more sustainable. International scientific cooperation, shared knowledge and innovation will remain important in shaping this progress. The story of space is, at its heart, a story of human curiosity, imagination and shared achievement. It is a journey that connects people everywhere through a common interest in discovering and understanding the universe. Every new discovery opens doors to further learning, while every technological advance creates possibilities for improving life on Earth. With knowledge, cooperation and a spirit of exploration, humanity can continue to move towards a future filled with discovery and opportunity. The universe remains vast, and there is still so much to learn, explore and understand. (The Author is a Columnist and can be reached at: bakshisuhaib094@gmail.com )

Every mission requires investment, specialised skills and careful preparation.
Each test adds to scientific understanding, with every outcome providing valuable lessons that help engineers develop better technologies.
As more objects enter orbit, advances in space monitoring and responsible practices can help make the space environment safer and more sustainable.
International scientific cooperation, shared knowledge and innovation will remain important in shaping this progress.
The story of space is, at its heart, a story of human curiosity, imagination and shared achievement.
It is a journey that connects people everywhere through a common interest in discovering and understanding the universe.
Every new discovery opens doors to further learning, while every technological advance creates possibilities for improving life on Earth.
With knowledge, cooperation and a spirit of exploration, humanity can continue to move towards a future filled with discovery and opportunity.
The universe remains vast, and there is still so much to learn, explore and understand.

stories.headline: Snowfall brings Gulmarg alive
stories.title: Snowfall brings Gulmarg alive
stories.summary: Baramulla, Nov 12: The season's first snowfall at the famous tourist resort of Gulmarg has brought cheer to visitors, offering them a glimpse of winter's magic as snow-covered mountain peaks transformed the landscape into a picturesque winter wonderland. Snowfall in the upper reaches of Kashmir overnight on Wednesday and continuing into Thursday brought a noticeable chill to the Valley, while Gulmarg's snow-draped slopes offered visitors a spectacular glimpse of the winter season. At Gulmarg, tourists were seen soaking in the beauty of the snow-covered mountains, with many stepping outdoors to experience the snowfall and capture the moment on their phones. The cold breeze, white mountain slopes and occasional snowflakes made the experience particularly memorable for visitors. Kongdori, a popular tourist destination accessible through the Gulmarg Gondola, received a good amount of snowfall, adding to the excitement among tourists. Visitors were seen enjoying the falling snowflakes, clicking photographs and capturing videos against the backdrop of the snow-clad mountains. For several tourists, witnessing snowfall was an experience they had been eagerly waiting for. Many described themselves as fortunate to have visited Gulmarg at a time when the first flakes of the season were falling, saying the unexpected winter spectacle had made their trip even more special. "Seeing snowfall for the first time is a great experience. We feel lucky to be among those who got the opportunity to witness it," said Yogesh, a tourist from West Bengal. A hotlier while talking to Greater Kashmir said that from the last two days, the tourist flow has abruptly increased. He said scores of vehicles full of tourists had thronged the Gulmarg and the fresh snowfall has drawn huge enthusiasm among the tourists. “The tourist flux has increased suddenly. The snowfall experience is always tourists first choice,” he said. The fresh snowfall has also added to Gulmarg's winter appeal, with the resort expected to attract more visitors as temperatures continue to fall. With the onset of winter and fresh snowfall, Gulmarg traditionally witnesses an increase in tourist arrivals, particularly among visitors keen to experience snow and enjoy the resort's scenic surroundings. Meanwhile, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast fairly widespread to widespread rainfall and snowfall across Jammu and Kashmir on November 12 and 13 under the influence of a western disturbance. The weather department has also warned of isolated heavy rainfall on Thursday, while thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds reaching 40-50 kmph, with gusts up to 60 kmph, are likely at isolated places. The IMD has forecast a significant fall in daytime temperatures, with the mercury expected to drop by 6-8 degrees Celsius during the two days. The precipitation is likely to continue over higher reaches, bringing further snowfall to the mountains.
